I.         BACKGROUND

                   A. Accounting for AROs and the Commission’s ARO Rate Regulations

        An ARO is a liability resulting from a legal obligation to retire or decommission a plant
asset. The Commission established accounting, reporting, and ratemaking rules concerning
AROs in Order No. 631.5

        For accounting and reporting, Order No. 631 required that companies “separately account
and report the liability for the asset retirement obligations, capitalize the asset retirement costs,
charge earnings for depreciation of the asset and charge operating expense for the accretion of
the liability.”6 This necessitated several changes to the Uniform System of Accounts and FERC
Form No. 1, including, for example and as is relevant here, the addition of an account (403.1) to
capture depreciation expense associated with asset retirement costs, and a “new Column (c)” on
the FERC Form 1 to report that same value. 7

        For ratemaking, Order No. 631 stated that “public utilities . . . with formula rate tariffs
must not include any cost components related to asset retirement obligations in their formula rate
billing tariffs for automatic recovery in their billing determinations without obtaining
Commission approval.”8 The Commission created a new regulation, 18 C.F.R. § 35.18, that sets
forth ratemaking rules around AROs. It (1) provides a categorical prohibition on ARO -related
cost components impacting the calculation of rate base and (2) requires utilities to remove all
ARO-related cost components from the rate, unless a utility files for and receives approval from
the Commission allowing for the recovery of such ARO-related cost components.

                   B. The Formula Rates Being Changed in This Proceeding

         EKC administers several cost-based wholesale power sale templates. These tariffs were
established by agreement with the relevant wholesale customers, 9 and have been modified from
time-to-time through rate filings. Through review of its formula rate templates, EKC has
identified certain formula rates that, if applied as drafted, would permit recovery of ARO-related
cost components and/or in certain circumstances have such cost components impact the
calculation of rate base. EKC does not believe that it was its own intent or the intent of any of
the settling parties to allow recovery of such costs, but rather believes the references were

II.       EVERGY PROPOSES CHANGES TO THE GFR AND MCPHERSON
          TEMPLATE TO ADDRESS THE ITEMS IDENTIFIED IN SECTION I.C, AND

                 A. Evergy Proposes Modifications to the GFR to Ensure No ARO-Related
                    Cost Components Impact the Calculation of Rate Base, Consistent with 18
                    C.F.R. § 35.18(a)

         18 C.F.R. § 35.18(a) provides that “all cost components related to asset retirement
obligations that would impact the calculation of rate base, such as electric plant and related
accumulated depreciation and accumulated deferred income taxes, may not be reflected in rates
and must be removed from the rate base calculation through a single adjustment.” 20 For the
GFR, as noted above, EKC (then Westar) partially complied with this requirement through its
filing in Docket No. ER14-805 to remove ARO-related cost components from the derivation of
“electric plant” in calculating the rate base. EKC did not, however, modify accumulated
depreciation, but proposes to do so through this filing. 21

        For the GFR, EKC proposes to resolve this issue with a more robust structure to exclude
AROs. It proposes to add a new section to the template, the “ARO Adjustment” section, to
determine both Plant in Service Net of AROs, and Accumulated Depreciation, Net of AROs, both
of which will feed into Item 3 - Rate Base to ensure that Rate Base components are only
calculated without reference to any ARO-related items. 22

                 B. Evergy Proposes Modifications to the GFR and McPherson Template to
                    Remove ARO Depreciation Expense Consistent with 18 C.F.R. § 35.18(c)

        The GFR and McPherson Template use inputs from EKC’s FERC Form No. 1 to
calculate depreciation expense. Specifically, the templates reference page 336 of the FERC
Form No. 1, which contains a summary of the depreciation and amortization charges, organized
into row by functional classification, for four FERC accounts: 403 Depreciation Expense (page
336 column b), 403.1 Depreciation Expense for Asset Retirement Costs (page 336 column c),
404 Amortization of Limited Term Electric Plant (page 336 column d), and 405 Amortization of
Other Electric Plant (page 336 column e). These columns are totaled in column f. 23

       Currently, each of the templates reference the total from column f, which includes the
amount reported (if any) in column c.24 Evergy proposes to revise these references to exclude
column c, thereby excluding Depreciation Expense for Asset Retirement Costs (Account 403.1).
To do this, Evergy proposes to update references to page 336 column f to reference page 336
columns b, d, and e only in the following manner:

              For the GFR Template, the “FERC Form 1 Data Inputs” tab at page 3, lines 103-109,
               and page 9, lines 103-109 (on the GFR Template, Evergy also proposes to update the
               labeling on the Item 4, Demand Related Expenses, page 3, to reflect the changes to
               the FERC Form 1 Data Inputs);25 and

              For the McPherson Template, the “FERC Form 1 Data Inputs” tab at lines 103-109. 26

       To the extent that any of these rows did not reference page 336 column f but did reference
page 336 column c, Evergy still proposes to update the column reference to columns b, d, and e
for consistency.27

        These modifications are consistent with 18 C.F.R. § 35.18(c), which provides that “[a]
public utility that has recorded asset retirement obligations on its books, but is not seeking
recovery of the asset retirement costs in rates, must remove all asset-retirement-obligations-
related cost components from the cost of service supporting its proposed rates.” Evergy is not
seeking recovery of these amounts, and never intended to recover them. It is therefore
modifying its formulas to ensure these amounts are automatically excluded.

                C. Evergy Proposes Modifications to the GFR and McPherson Templates to
                   Ensure ARO-Related Costs Do Not Impact Allocation Percentages,
                   Consistent with 18 C.F.R. § 35.18(c)

        Given the breadth of 18 C.F.R. § 35.18(c), Evergy believes it is reasonable to also
exclude any ARO-related costs from the derivation of allocators which then influence formula
rate calculations. While not binding on Evergy, Evergy understands that Commission audit staff
has taken this view for another entity.28 Therefore, Evergy proposes changes to certain of the
formula rate templates to ensure that ARO amounts are not included as a component of an
allocation percentage.

                  1.      Changes to GFR Template

        Evergy proposes to revise the GFR Template to ensure that AROs are not included in the
allocation ratios. To calculate the allocation ratios on Worksheet C, the GFR Template pulls
inputs from Item 3 - Rate Base, including Total Production Plant in Service [Item 3, line 1] and
Production Accumulated Depreciation [Item 3, line 2]. The current GFR Template excludes
AROs from Total Production Plant by subtracting out ARO accounts on Item 3 - Rate Base. It
does not, however, subtract ARO accounts out of the Accumulated Depreciation calculation—
thus ARO amounts have been included in the allocation ratios via Production Accumulated
Depreciation. Evergy proposes to resolve this issue with a more robust structure to exclude
AROs. It proposes to add a new section, ARO Adjustment, to determine Net Plant Net of
AROs.29 Item 3 - Rate Base will pull inputs from ARO Adjustment and there will be no need to
subtract ARO accounts in the Rate Base section to ensure that AROs are excluded. 30 The Rate
Base section will pull from the ARO Adjustment section to calculate Accumulated Depreciation,
and this will ensure that Accumulated Depreciation is calculated net of AROs.

      Evergy also proposes to revise two items on Worksheet C to pull from the new ARO
Adjustment section, Total Plant in Service Net of AROs [ARO Adj, pg. 2, lines 1-7] and Total
Accumulated Depreciation Net of AROs [ARO Adj, pg. 2, lines 8-14]. 31

        Finally, the new ARO Adjustment section requires inputs from FERC Form No. 1 data
that are not presently used in the GFR Template. Therefore, Evergy proposes to add these new
inputs to FERC Form No. 1 Data Inputs at pg. 1, lines 30a-30d, pg. 2, lines 39a-39b, and pg. 7,
lines 30a-30d, 39a-39b.32

                  2.     Changes to the McPherson Template

        Evergy proposes to revise the McPherson Template to ensure that AROs are not included
in the allocation ratios. In the Rate Calculation sections, Exhibit I pages 5-9, Evergy proposes
changes in three different sections to remove AROs from the calculation inputs. First, on page 7,
section 4, lines b and c, Evergy proposes to update the inputs for Total Steam Production Plant
and Total Steam Production Accumulated Reserve to make these inputs net of AROs. 33 This will
ensure AROs are removed from the allocation factor calculation in section 4, line e and the ADIT
calculation section 4, line g. Second, on page 8, section 6, line b, Evergy proposes to update the
input for Total Electric Plant in Service to make it net of AROs. 34 This will ensure that AROs are
removed from the Calculated Property Tax Rate [page 8, section 6, line c] and, in turn, the
calculation of the Annual Revenue Requirement [page 6, line 28]. Third, on page 9, section 7,
line g, Evergy proposes to update Total Steam Production Plant to make it net of AROs. 35 This
will ensure that AROs are excluded from the ITC Amortization Expense allocation factor [page
9, section 7, line h] and, in turn, the calculation of Annual Revenue Requirements [page 6, line
28].

        The proposed changes to the Rate Calculation sections require data inputs from FERC
Form No. 1 that are not currently used in the McPherson Template. Therefore, Evergy is
proposing to add these inputs to FERC Form No. 1 Data Inputs: line 28a-28c, lines 30a-30d, and
line 35a.36

UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                               BEFORE THE
                 FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


                                     ATTACHMENT A
                        DECLARATION OF JOHN WOLFRAM

I.   INTRODUCTION AND QUALIFICATIONS

     1. My name is John Wolfram. I am the founder and Principal of Catalyst Consulting LLC,
        a rate and regulatory consulting firm. My business address is 3308 Haddon Road,
        Louisville, Kentucky, 40241.

     2. I received the degree of Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering from the
        University of Notre Dame in South Bend, Indiana, in May 1990. I also received the
        Master of Science degree in Electrical Engineering from Drexel University in
        Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, in June 1997, with a concentration in power system
        modeling and engineering management.

     3. I began my career in 1990 with PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”), where I
        implemented Energy Management Systems (“EMS”) for the reliable operation of the
        multi-state transmission grid. I left PJM to work with Cincinnati Gas & Electric
        Company in 1993 on an EMS project before returning to PJM in 1994 during the
        deregulation of the electric wholesale market. I implemented new practices and tools
        for PJM in conjunction with Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“Commission”
        or “FERC”) Order Nos. 888 and 889. In 1997, I joined Louisville Gas & Electric
        Company (“LG&E”). I worked in Energy Trading and Generation Planning before
        becoming the Manager of Regulatory Affairs for LG&E and Kentucky Utilities
        Company (“KU”). In that role, I directed strategic regulatory initiatives with the FERC
        and with regulators in Kentucky and Virginia, including rate cases, certificates of
        public convenience and necessity and transmission siting proceedings, compliance &
        management audits, regional transmission organization (“RTO”) membership, and
        hydroelectric relicensing. I testified many times before the Kentucky Public Service
        Commission and participated as a panelist in a FERC technical conference on
        Standards of Conduct. I then served as Director of Customer Service & Marketing for
        LG&E and KU, where I was responsible for all facets of customer interaction, including
        marketing, major accounts, walk-in offices, call centers, customer inquiries, economic
        development, and energy efficiency program design and implementation.

     4. In 2009, I joined The Prime Group, LLC, a rate and regulatory consulting firm, as a
        Senior Consultant. In that role, I provided consulting services to investor-owned
        utilities, municipal utilities, and electric cooperatives on matters related to rate design,
        formula rates, cost of service studies, revenue requirements, open access transmission
        tariffs, RTO membership, and special rate structures. In 2012, I founded Catalyst
        Consulting LLC, a rate and regulatory consulting firm specializing in utility rate cases,
        tariffs, transmission formula rates, and complex regulatory matters.


                                               1
         5. In my current role I provide consulting services to electric utilities on matters relating
           to rate design, cost of service, revenue requirements, special rate structures, and other
           regulatory matters. I have provided advice on pricing matters and rate design to several
           transmission-only entities as well as to traditional investor-owned utilities, electric
           cooperatives, and municipal utilities. I have advised utilities on transmission issues
           associated with FERC regulation of open access transmission service. I have provided
           consulting services to transmission-owning members of the Midcontinent Independent
           System Operator, Inc., PJM, and Southwest Power Pool, Inc. I have advised these
           clients on transmission formula rates, transmission pricing, transmission planning, cost
           allocation, and other broad transmission policy initiatives. I have also performed cost
           of service studies and retail rate design for numerous regulated and unregulated
           distribution-only utilities across the country.

        6. I am submitting this declaration on behalf of Evergy Kansas Central, Inc. (“EKC”),
           Evergy Metro, Inc. (“EMe”), Prairie Wind Transmission, LLC (“PWT”), and Evergy
           Missouri West, Inc. (“EMW“) (together, “Evergy” or the “Evergy Companies”).1 The
           purpose of my declaration is to describe Evergy’s proposed revisions to its formula rate
           templates to remove costs related to Asset Retirement Obligations (“AROs”) from
           several Evergy formula rate templates and explain why I believe the changes and
           resulting formulas are consistent with the Commission’s rules and policies regarding
           AROs.

        7. I have prepared the following exhibits in support of this declaration:

                             i. Exhibit No. JW-01, Summary of Proposed Revisions to EKC’s
                                Generation Formula Rate;2

                            ii. Exhibit No. JW-02, Summary of Proposed Revisions to EKC’s
                                McPherson Formula Rate;

                           iii. Exhibit No. JW-03, Summary of Proposed Revisions to EKC’s
                                Transmission Formula Rate;

                            iv. Exhibit No. JW-04, Summary of Proposed Revisions to EMe’s
                                Transmission Formula Rate;

                            v. Exhibit No. JW-05, Summary of Proposed Revisions to EMW’s
                               Transmission Formula Rate; and

                            vi. Exhibit No. JW-06, Summary of Proposed Revisions to PWT’s
                                Transmission Formula Rate.


    1
     I understand that my same declaration is being included in two separate filings—one for EKC’s
generation rates, and one for EKC, EMe, PWT, and EMW’s transmission rates.
    2
     Because the amended GFR tariff sheets in each of these rate schedules are identical, EKC is submitting
one clean copy of the GFR summary.


                                                    2
 II.        BACKGROUND

           8. AROs are liabilities resulting from a legal obligation to retire or decommission a plant
              asset. They are quite common in the electric industry, in particular for entities that own
              generation. They are intended to ensure that entities recognize that a future liability
              exists regarding certain current assets (i.e., plant assets).

           9. The Commission has specific rules regarding accounting, reporting, and ratemaking
              associated with AROs. This declaration is concerned with the Commission’s
              ratemaking requirements. In particular, the Commission’s regulations prohibit ARO-
              related cost components from impacting the calculation of rate base in all instances and
              require that utilities remove all ARO-related cost components from rates unless they
              have received specific authorization to include such cost components in rates.3

           10. The Evergy Companies administer several different formula rates that are calculated
               using, at least in part, values reported on the FERC Form No. 1 (“FF1”) for the
               respective Evergy Company. Evergy has reviewed these templates and determined that
               certain formula rates, as currently effective, permit recovery of ARO-related cost
               components in rates. I believe it is an open question whether the Commission’s
               approval of templates that permit such recovery qualifies as the specific authorization
               envisioned by 18 C.F.R. § 35.18 (2026), but it is my understanding that Evergy never
               intended to recover these balances and is now making this filing to modify the
               templates to ensure that these balances are automatically excluded in the formula rate
               process.

           11. My testimony below goes through each template that is being changed and discusses
               the particular changes that are being made and how those changes ensure that no ARO-
               related costs are included in the calculation of rates.

III.       PROPOSED REVISIONS TO THE GENERATION FORMULA RATE
           TEMPLATES

           A.     Changes to GFR Template

           12. In the current GFR template, ARO-related cost components may impact the calculation
               of Rate Base, the calculation of Depreciation Expense, and the derivation of allocators
               that are used to allocate certain costs that are not specific to the generation function.
               Rate Base is determined on Item 3 – Rate Base. Depreciation Expense is determined
               on Item 4 – Demand-Related Expenses, page 2 of 3. The allocators for Gross Plant in
               Service and Net Plant in Service are determined on Worksheet C, Allocation Ratios.
               As the formula rate currently exists today, none of these items are explicitly calculated



       3
      18 C.F.R. § 35.18; see also Acct., Fin. Reporting, & Rate Filing Requirements for Asset Retirement
Obligations, Order No. 631, 103 FERC ¶ 61,021 (2003); order on reh’g, Order No. 631-A, 104 FERC
¶ 61,183 (2003) (establishing prohibition on ARO-related cost components of rates).


                                                    3
                net of AROs.4 The template also has worksheets for data entry of values from the FF1,
               which currently do not include fields for the entry of ARO amounts from the FF1.

          13. Evergy proposes revising items on these worksheets to ensure that FF1 data pertaining
              to AROs is shown in the template and that Rate Base, Depreciation Expense, and the
              allocators for Gross Plant in Service and Net Plant in Service are calculated net of
              AROs. Please refer to Exhibit No. JW-01 for a line-by-line description of the proposed
              revisions.

          14. First, Evergy proposes to revise the worksheets for FF1 Inputs and FF1 Inputs
              (Transition Year) to add rows for the entry of ARO data from the FF1. For both sheets
              this includes lines 30a – 30f, for both the item descriptions and the corresponding FF1
              references. Evergy also clarifies the references to the FF1 for other plant listed on lines
              103-109.

          15. Second, Evergy proposes the addition of Worksheet ARO Adj which calculates
              amounts for Gross Plant in Service, Accumulated Depreciation, and Net Plant in
              Service net of AROs. The worksheet mirrors that already included in the EKC TFR
              Template discussed later.5 The worksheet shows gross values and ARO values for each
              line item and calculates the difference for each line item which is the amount net of
              AROs.

          16. Third, Evergy proposes to revise Item 3 – Rate Base to remove the current lines that
              subtract ARO amounts and instead to revise the lines related to Plant in Service and
              Accumulated Depreciation to reflect amounts net of AROs, with references to the
              appropriate fields on the new Worksheet ARO Adj. The phrase “Net of AROs” is
              added to the lines that sum to Plant in Service and to Accumulated Depreciation for the
              columns that pertain to EKC and EKS.

          17. Fourth, Evergy proposes to revise Item 4 – Demand-Related Expenses, page 2, to
              correct the source of the amounts entered in the columns for EKC and EKS to ensure
              that they properly reference Depreciation Expense items in the FF1 calculated net of
              AROs.

          18. Fifth, Evergy proposes to revise Worksheet C – Allocation Ratios to include new lines
              for Total Plant in Service Net of AROs and Total Accumulated Depreciation Net of
              AROs, both with references to the appropriate fields on the new Worksheet ARO Adj.
              Evergy also proposes to include the phrase “Net of AROs” in the headers for Gross
              Plant, Net Plant and Energy Storage Plant in this section on page 1.



    4
      18 C.F.R. § 35.18 also specifies the AROs should be excluded from Accumulated Deferred Income
Taxes (“ADIT”). Under the current template, though, Evergy can (and my understanding is that they do)
exclude these balances so that they do not impact the calculation of the rate. Because the existing template
already has a mechanism to address this issue, Evergy proposes no changes regarding ADIT.
    5
        See infra ¶ 27.


                                                     4
 19. The proposed revisions explicitly remove ARO amounts noted on the FF1 from the
    determination of Rate Base and from the Depreciation Expense amounts used in the
